newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan president quits, sees FY97 loss.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan president quits, sees FY97 loss.

text.p: Donna Karan International Inc said Thursday that Stephen Ruzow had resigned as president and chief operating officer, effective immediately.
The company said Ruzow also would resign as a company director but continue as a consultant for the next six months.
Additionally, the company said it expects to report a loss of $0.55 per share or greater for fiscal 1997, excluding potential additional charges.
The company based its projection on first half results, which showed a $0.64 per share loss.

It also cited poor sales of the Spring season DKNY Womens and Donna Karan New York Mens collections at retail, below budgeted growth in DKNY Mens sales and below-plan performance of its Beauty division.
It also cited deferral of the launch of DKNY Mens and Womens Jeans to the first quarter of 1998 and weaker-than-expected comparable store sales at the outlet stores.
The company is planning a deal involving a license, sale or joint venture for its Beauty division and said Thursday that it expects to announce such a deal in the third quarter.
